headline: High-risk shared-state orchestration: LangGraph can write shared checkpointer state while Prefect broad network egress creates leakage and cascading-action risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can write application-defined files and uses a shared checkpointer store; Prefect can consume workflow metadata and broad network egress means attacker-controlled content could traverse the pair. The pathway is plausible in default orchestration setups, though not proven to be a direct parser hijack. Both agents contribute to the bridge.
conditions: IF Prefect ingests LangGraph-produced workflow state or files as instructions without validation
IF the shared checkpointer stores attacker-controlled content that later reaches Prefect parsing logic
mitigations: Add provenance tags to all shared state entries
Require schema validation before Prefect consumes LangGraph outputs
Separate the checkpointer namespace per agent
Disable free-form text fields in shared workflow metadata
requires-engineering: add content-signing for inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph explicitly handles model provider API keys and writes application-defined files; Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad network egress. A shared workspace or checkpointer could expose sensitive graph state to Prefect and onward over the network. This is not provably blocked by either profile, so the safer medium rating applies.
conditions: IF the shared checkpointer contains secrets or sensitive graph state
IF Prefect serializes workflow metadata to an external service or API
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared graph state
Restrict Prefect to redacted metadata only
Rotate any API keys present in shared state
Use separate storage backends for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce field-level encryption on shared state

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph has write_filesystem, execute_shell, subprocess, and broad network egress; Prefect also has broad network egress and is an orchestration system that can mutate workflow state. Even without explicit git scopes, overlapping write and network authority on shared resources creates a dangerous conflict surface in default orchestration patterns.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same writable workspace or shared state backend
IF Prefect tasks and LangGraph nodes can mutate the same workflow artifacts concurrently
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories or buckets
Serialize writes through a single coordinator
Disable shell execution for one agent
Use optimistic-locking on shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add distributed locks around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is a low-level orchestration framework that can emit state and outputs, while Prefect is an automation/orchestration system that may act on workflow metadata. If Prefect treats LangGraph output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or incorrect automation. The pairwise interaction is therefore hazardous by default unless explicit verification is added.
conditions: IF Prefect uses LangGraph-produced state as an input without independent validation
IF downstream Prefect flows trigger actions based on LangGraph-generated facts
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require human approval for action-taking flows
Limit LangGraph output to structured, typed records
Log and diff all handoffs between agents
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and touch workflow/graph metadata rather than a regulated data class, so no direct residency or certification mismatch is evidenced. However, LangGraph handles model provider API keys and Prefect has broad network egress, so a compliance gap could arise if sensitive metadata is routed externally. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared workflow metadata
IF external network calls carry that metadata across jurisdictions
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared metadata
Document data-flow boundaries for both agents
Redact secrets before handoff
Restrict outbound endpoints to approved services
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
